p:Lax606786Proofs.bernsteinNumber_nonneg.label:
Either no `k`-dimensional subspace exists, and the supremum of the empty set is `0`, or every
growth in the supremum is nonnegative.

p:Lax606786Proofs.bernsteinNumber_one.label:
`ρ_1(T) = ‖T‖`: the Bernstein supremum over lines is the operator norm. Both sides are `0`
when `X` is trivial, where there are no lines at all.

p:Lax606786Proofs.bernsteinNumber_zero.label:
`ρ_0(T) = 0`: the only `0`-dimensional subspace is `⊥`, on which `T` vanishes identically,
so every member of the defining range is `g_T(⊥) = 0`.

Consequently `χ_0 = -∞`, which is why the statements about `χ_k` are for `k ≥ 1`; the case
`k = 0` is recorded because `Cocycle.exists_chi_ae_const` is stated for all `k`.
